What you can do today

Whiteboard items 0 to 3 are built end to end, from the database to the screen.

  • 0Tags

    Four presets on first visit: Pay cheque and Side hustle for money in, Bill and Groceries for money out. Any colour from a styled picker (swatches, a hue slider, a hex field); rename or delete leaves a tag's streams untagged instead of breaking them. Each tag has its own page listing every stream that carries it.

  • 1Income and expense streams

    Add, edit, and delete money on a rhythm: a name, the usual amount, how often (Weekly, Every 2 weeks, Monthly, or every N days), a next date from a styled calendar, and an optional tag. "Add a range" folds open a minimum and maximum when a stream is not fixed. Expense amounts are expense-orange everywhere.

  • 2The balance check-in

    The first thing on the overview: type today's balance and Save, and a "Saved" line confirms it while the forecast redraws. Every check-in is kept; the balances page flips through them, redraws the forecast from any of them, and says how each compared with what the previous one expected.

  • 3The overview

    A sentence answers "am I going to be OK?" first ("You go $255 short on Oct 2. You are under zero from Oct 2 until Oct 11."), then the chart: a dot per payment, the band from worst to best case, the time under zero shaded expense-orange. Three small tiles below hold the lowest point, the expected end balance, and the worst-to-best range. Coming up lists the month's payments by day, with a switcher to flip months and a "Today" divider.

Also working: sign up, sign in, and sign out, with every /app page behind sign-in; the landing page, updated for this iteration; a top bar on desktop and a bottom tab bar on phones; an install manifest for the phone app.

Landing page

The balance check-in

The first thing on the overview: type today's balance and Save, and "Saved" confirms it while the forecast redraws.

Overview, 30 days

The sentence leads: "You go $255 short on Oct 2. You are under zero from Oct 2 until Oct 11." Money in is green, money out and the time under zero are expense-orange.

Overview, 90 days, with Coming up

At 90 days the same sentence and chart, with Coming up below: this month's payments by day, a switcher to flip to next month, and a "Today" divider.

The worst case dips below $0 from Oct 2 to Oct 11, when Rent and the bills land before enough café shifts have paid; the chart shades that stretch expense-orange.

Adding a stream

Name, usual amount, how often, and a next date from a styled calendar; "Add a range" folds open a minimum and maximum for streams that are not fixed, and becomes "Remove the range" once it is. The Tag select also offers "New tag…" to make one without leaving the form.

Each stream as a card with its amount, how often, and next date; expense amounts are expense-orange, income amounts are green.

How it works

Streams, not receipts

Every income and expense is a stream: a name, an optional tag, three amounts (minimum ≤ usual ≤ maximum), a repeat interval of 1 to 366 days, and a next payment date. The form only ever asks for the usual amount; minimum and maximum default to it and only appear once "Add a range" is opened. Amounts out of order are refused with a message on the field, and nothing is saved.

The forecast rule

A stream pays on firstDate + k × intervalDays for k = 0, 1, 2, and so on. The forecast always starts from the latest balance check-in and rolls forward to today, so it never goes stale. Each day gets three balances:

  • Worst case: every income at its minimum, every expense at its maximum.
  • Expected: everything at its usual amount.
  • Best case: incomes at their maximum, expenses at their minimum.

The overview leads with the answer in words: the lowest point of the expected line, and when (if ever) it recovers.

Presets

The first time someone opens the app, four tags are created for them: two for money in, two for money out.

  • Pay cheque
  • Side hustle
  • Bill
  • Groceries

Where the data lives

One Postgres database: tags, income streams, expense streams, and every balance check-in a person has saved, with every query limited to the signed-in person. The browser only ever talks to the SvelteKit server, which fetches from the Express API with the session cookie; that keeps the door open for an offline-capable phone app. Accounts are email and password through Better Auth.

Money is cents

Every amount is stored and sent as whole cents (110000 is $1,100.00), so nothing drifts by a fraction of a cent; the screens show dollars with two decimals in Canadian format. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and all date math runs in UTC.

The API

Every route needs the session cookie and answers 401 when signed out; bad input gets 400 naming the field that failed, and a missing row 404.

MethodPathSendGet back
GET/api/tagsnone{ tags }; creates the 4 presets on first call
POST/api/tagsname, color?201 the new tag
PATCH/api/tags/:idname?, color?the updated tag
DELETE/api/tags/:idnone204; its streams become untagged
GET/api/income-streamsnone{ streams }
POST/api/income-streamsname, tagId?, minCents?, actualCents, maxCents?, intervalDays, firstDate201 the new stream; min and max default to the usual amount
PATCH/api/income-streams/:idany of the abovethe updated stream
DELETE/api/income-streams/:idnone204
Same 4/api/expense-streams[/:id]same as incomesame as income
GET/api/checkinsnone{ checkins }, newest first
POST/api/checkinsbalanceCents201 the check-in, always dated today; a second save the same day replaces it
GET/api/forecastdays 7 to 366, checkinId?one point per day (worst, expected, best), every event, the end balance, the lowest point, and when the balance goes under and recovers
GET/api/coming-upmonth? YYYY-MMthe month's events by day, with totals in, out, and the expected end balance

Also there: GET /api/health (open, for the deploy), GET /api/me, sign-up and sign-in under /api/auth/*, and interactive docs at /api/docs.

Iteration 2 shipped the overview sentence, the check-in habit, styled forms and colours, and tag pages. What is left, in the order the iteration 2 proposal puts it.

Statement import

L
In the model
A PDF statement or paystub, parsed on the box only, stripped to dates, amounts, and categories, turned into suggested streams that Sam accepts or discards. A stream is exactly what that detector produces, so the model needs no change. Planned in docs/plans/2026-09-27-statement-import-plan.md.
On screen
Upload a statement, review the suggested streams next to what they were parsed from, accept or discard each one.
Smallest demo
One paystub, parsed into one suggested income stream that Sam accepts as is.

Open questions for the two of you

  • Does a goal belong to the whole balance or to a tag? The whole balance matches today's forecast and is simplest; a tag such as Savings means money has to be set aside for it.
  • When a check-in differs from the forecast, should kriket guess why? (“Groceries cost $30 more than usual this month.”) Proposed for a later iteration: only the difference for now, no guessing.
  • Statement import: when, and what is kept? Open; the plan file stands with its four decisions (scope, retention, timing, statement or paystub first) unanswered until this iteration is reviewed.
